Mar 16, 2017 15:21:09 GMT -5 clonem said:
That rare, underrated species looks to me like N. rigidifolia. However, it almost looks like a hybrid, but with Josh's knowledge, probably not.

At the very least a rigidifolia hybrid (a lot of them recently have turned out to be spectabilis crosses). The pure species is quite distinct, and I'd hold my doubts on that one, but possible.

And to the other sudden trend on this thread: anyone to drop a bomb in one of my Neps would soon find reaper peppers up the distribution center; I'll hold a well-grown mature Nepenthes hamata over most Sarrs any day

Awesome pics Little Mikey! Thanks again for stopping by.

Mar 15, 2017 19:49:40 GMT -5 hcarlton said:
The questioned hybrid or species: ventricosa x ephippiata. And if that one plant is indeed stably variegated it's a special one; I have a lingulata seedling that has remained variegated for over 3 years now, and is finally getting somewhere in size.
Not quite. It's N. lowii x merrilliana.

I have a few stable variegated Nepenthes. The pictured one (N. densiflora x robcantleyi) came from Borneo Exotics like that, but the variegation seems to be fading with each leaf. It was likely an environmental thing, but I'm holding onto it to make sure.
